newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rice prices rise 10 percent - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rice prices rise 10 percent - newspaper.

text.p: Retail prices for rice in Singapore have risen by up to 10 percent over the past two months because of strong rice prices in the international market, the Straits Times newspaper said on Thursday.
"To this day, FairPrice is still absorbing the cost increases," S. Chandra Das, chairman of retail chain NTUC Fairprice's board of directors, said in remarks reported by the paper.
"We will hold the prices for as long as we can until such a time as it becomes impossible for us to do so," he said.
The chain, one of the leading retail outlets in Singapore, buys over 99 percent of its rice from Thailand, the world's leading exporter of the staple.
Chandra Das said the firm has imported one container of Burmese rice as an alternative to Thai rice.
"If it proves popular, we can continue to bring in more Myanmar (Burma) rice," he said. "We cannot be too dependent on one (supplier)."
